candidates.title: Mine repeat-run instability into targeted memory guidelines
candidates.rule: For recurring API workflows, compare guidelines mined from unstable decision points with the unchanged agent, evaluating both average success and all-run consistency.
candidates.passage: a confidently-wrong decision looks consistent to it.
candidates.location: Section 6 limitations; Section 7 and Appendix B tables
candidates.finding: On AppWorld ReAct/GPT-4.1, similar-task guidelines raise all-five-run success from 53.0% to 66.0% and mean success from 77.4% to 79.5%. Hard-task mean success slightly declines, despite improved consistency.
candidates.conditions: Offline analyzer resamples each inference step thirty times; guidelines are committed to episodic memory and retrieved for later similar tasks.
candidates.limitations: The analyzer is not a verifier. Repeatedly wrong behavior can be stable. Admission validation is proposed future work and not implemented in the tested pipeline. Roughly thirtyfold analysis token overhead and platform nondeterminism matter.
candidates.validation_test: Generate guidelines from development traces; compare on untouched similar tasks over repeated runs. Report all-run success, mean success, stable errors, subgroup regressions and offline analysis cost.
